nature-pol-255.q: How did the 1977 offset mechanism work?
nature-pol-255.a: A firm could emit more if it paid another firm to cut the same pollutant.

nature-pol-250.q: Why can carbon trading leave local air pollution in place?
nature-pol-250.a: Schemes cap only greenhouse gases, so factories can buy permits instead of cutting local pollution.

nature-pol-241.q: Who gains when carbon money is returned per person?
nature-pol-241.a: Richer people with bigger footprints pay more, and poorer people can come out ahead.

nature-pol-273.q: How much discretion does this reserve mechanism allow?
nature-pol-273.a: None: it runs on predefined rules with no discretion for the Commission or member states.

nature-pol-283.q: Why do companies and individuals buy these credits?
nature-pol-283.a: To compensate voluntarily for their emissions; each one equals 1 tonne of CO2.

nature-pol-260.q: What must a polluter affecting several monitoring points hold?
nature-pol-260.a: A portfolio of licences covering all of them.

nature-pol-205.q: What forms can a subsidy take?
nature-pol-205.a: Direct spending, tax incentives, cheap loans, price support and government-provided goods and services.

nature-pol-221.q: What kinds of goods does fair trade focus on?
nature-pol-221.a: Goods exported from poorer to richer countries, such as coffee, cocoa, handicrafts, fruit and gold.

nature-pol-194.q: How does making producers responsible push greener design?
nature-pol-194.a: Producers who pay end-of-life costs have a money incentive to design greener products.

nature-pol-208.q: How can a subsidy become perverse?
nature-pol-208.a: By not being withdrawn after it has reached its goal.

nature-pol-229.q: Do these standards concern the product itself?
nature-pol-229.a: No; like ISO 9000, they concern how a product or service is made.

nature-pol-220.q: Who can join this EU scheme?
nature-pol-220.a: Any type of organisation worldwide; it is voluntary.

nature-pol-198.q: Why are IMF subsidy estimates much larger than others?
nature-pol-198.a: Because they count unpriced externalities, unlike the OECD and IEA definitions.

nature-pol-185.q: How does ISO develop sustainability standards?

nature-pol-217.q: What changed in 2011 for qualifying products?
nature-pol-217.a: Instead of manufacturers' own data, which was open to fraud, independent labs and certifiers must test them.

nature-pol-193.q: What do critics say fossil fuel subsidies do?
nature-pol-193.a: Raise consumption and waste, burden public finances and hold back cleaner technologies.

nature-pol-214.q: What happens to farmers who fail cross compliance?

nature-pol-236.q: What does the Marine Stewardship Council do?
nature-pol-236.a: It runs a certification program for consumer seafood products.

nature-pol-018.q: What does environmental policy aim to do?
nature-pol-018.a: Steer human activity to prevent harm to the environment and to people.

nature-pol-020.q: Why are market instruments often promoted?
nature-pol-020.a: As a more efficient, cost-effective alternative to regulation.

nature-pol-023.q: Give an example of integrating environment into other policy.
nature-pol-023.a: Fuel taxes aimed at local pollution, or removing fossil fuel subsidies.

nature-pol-029.q: Why do market instruments give firms more flexibility?
nature-pol-029.a: They do not dictate technology or equal cuts for every firm.

nature-pol-042.q: What is Robert Shiller's classic example of rent-seeking?
nature-pol-042.a: A landowner who chains a river and charges boats to lower the chain, adding no value.

nature-pol-035.q: How has the fossil fuel lobby affected policy?
nature-pol-035.a: It promotes climate change denial and obstructs environmental and climate policy.

nature-pol-041.q: Why do technical industries risk cultural capture?
nature-pol-041.a: Regulators must hire experts who mostly come from the industry itself.

nature-pol-007.q: Which agreement officially set up the WTO?
nature-pol-007.a: The Marrakesh Agreement, signed on 15 April 1994 at the end of the Uruguay Round.

nature-pol-008.q: When may WTO members restrict trade?
nature-pol-008.a: To protect the environment or public, animal and plant health, but not as disguised protectionism.

nature-pol-004.q: How do tariffs differ in cost from testing or labelling rules?
nature-pol-004.a: Tariffs raise costs that grow with volume; testing or labelling rules impose fixed costs.

nature-pol-016.q: Why does the UN restrict trade in plastic waste?
nature-pol-016.a: Importing countries often lack the capacity to process all of it.

nature-mkt-136.q: Which three services draw most PES money?
nature-mkt-136.a: Climate change mitigation, watershed services and biodiversity conservation.

nature-mkt-137.q: Which idea is PES rooted in, according to environmental economics?
nature-mkt-137.a: The Coase theorem: a voluntary, conditional deal between a service buyer and seller.

nature-mkt-140.q: Did paying forest owners reduce deforestation?
nature-mkt-140.a: Yes: 2 to 5% in participating villages against 7 to 10% in control villages.

nature-mkt-152.q: What do most PES programmes pay for?
nature-mkt-152.a: Management practices; only less commonly measured outcomes.

nature-mkt-129.q: What are the steps of the mitigation hierarchy?

nature-mkt-124.a: A site where wetland projects are done before the damage they compensate for, producing credits developers can buy.

nature-mkt-121.q: Does funding general research count as a biodiversity offset?
nature-mkt-121.a: No; activities without a measurable gain for biodiversity do not count.

nature-mkt-126.q: How is US mitigation-bank land protected?
nature-mkt-126.a: By a conservation easement that also binds future owners of the land.

nature-mkt-104.q: Why did industrialised countries buy CDM credits?
nature-mkt-104.a: Because cutting emissions was cheapest in developing countries.

nature-mkt-090.q: What did the 2016 Öko-Institut study find about CDM projects?
nature-mkt-090.a: 85% were unlikely to be truly additional or likely overestimated reductions.

nature-mkt-108.q: What do the safeguards bar REDD+ actions from being used for?

nature-mkt-088.q: What do soil carbon projects try to do?
nature-mkt-088.a: Keep or raise the carbon stored in soil.

nature-mkt-091.q: Who created the Gold Standard, and why?
nature-mkt-091.a: WWF and partners in 2003, to make sure credits are real, verifiable and help sustainable development.

nature-mkt-114.q: What monitoring systems are REDD+ countries encouraged to build?
nature-mkt-114.a: Transparent systems combining satellite remote sensing with ground forest inventories.

nature-mkt-103.q: What did the January 2023 investigation find about Verra rainforest credits?
nature-mkt-103.a: About 94% did not represent a real tonne of CO2e.

nature-mkt-065.a: Borrowers' long-term investments, or for governments, current spending.

nature-mkt-056.q: Can loans count as official development assistance?
nature-mkt-056.a: Yes, soft loans count if their grant element is at least 25%; most aid is grants.

nature-mkt-049.a: Public and private funds in one deal, each party using its expertise.

nature-mkt-029.q: What are the main causes of biodiversity loss?
nature-mkt-029.a: Habitat loss, land-use change, pollution and overexploitation.

nature-mkt-015.a: When protecting one place pushes damaging activity to another, cutting the net benefit.

nature-mkt-057.q: Which countries first met the aid target, and when?
